subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Joseph interprets a Dream
overview: In Genesis 41:14-24 and 28-30, Pharaoh tells Joseph two dreams and Joseph says that only God can give the meaning. In this sub-strand you will retell that account, learn to depend on God's wisdom, and recite Proverbs 1:7 about the fear of the LORD.

lessons.title: Pharaoh's dreams and Joseph's answer
objectives: State what the dreams meant according to verses 28-30.
lessons.intro: Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had dreams that troubled him. None of his magicians could explain them. He sent for Joseph, who was brought from the prison.
lessons.notes:
Read Genesis 41:14-24 and 28-30 in turns. Stay inside those verses when you retell the story.

### Joseph is brought to Pharaoh
Pharaoh sent for Joseph. Joseph was brought quickly from the dungeon. He shaved, changed his clothes, and came in. Pharaoh said he had dreamed a dream and no one could interpret it. He had heard that Joseph could interpret a dream when he heard it.

Joseph answered, "I cannot do it, but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires."

### The two dreams
Pharaoh said he stood on the bank of the Nile. Seven fat, healthy cows came up and grazed. Then seven thin, ugly cows came up and ate the seven fat cows, but they still looked thin. He woke up.

He slept again and saw seven full, good heads of grain growing on one stalk. Then seven thin heads, scorched by the east wind, sprouted and swallowed the seven good heads. He told the magicians, and none of them could explain it.

### The meaning in verses 28-30
Joseph said that God had shown Pharaoh what He was about to do. Seven years of great plenty were coming in Egypt. After them would come seven years of famine. The famine would be so severe that the years of plenty would be forgotten, and the famine would ruin the land.

The passage you are reading does not include later advice about storing grain. Do not add it. What these verses teach is clear: God showed the seven good years and the seven years of famine, and Joseph would not take the credit.

Draw Joseph standing before Pharaoh and colour the picture. Dramatise the moment Joseph says that he himself cannot interpret the dream.

keyWords.meaning: a long, severe lack of food
the title of the king of Egypt
the prison from which Joseph was brought

activity.title: Read and dramatise the dreams
steps: Dramatise Joseph before Pharaoh, including Joseph's words that he cannot interpret the dream but God will give the answer.
Draw and colour Joseph standing before Pharaoh.
Retell the two dreams and their meaning without adding events from other verses.

practice.question: Where was Joseph brought from, and what did he do before he saw Pharaoh?
practice.answer: He was brought from the dungeon. He shaved and changed his clothes.

practice.question: What did Joseph say when Pharaoh asked him to interpret the dream?
practice.answer: He said he could not do it, but God would give Pharaoh the answer.

practice.question: What did the dreams mean in Genesis 41:28-30?
practice.answer: Seven years of great plenty would come in Egypt, followed by seven years of famine.

summary: Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat cows and seven thin cows, and of seven good heads of grain and seven thin ones.
Joseph said he could not interpret the dream, but God would.
The meaning was seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine.

lessons.title: Depending on God's wisdom
objectives: Explain how Joseph depended on God's wisdom.
Apply that lesson when he or she does not know an answer.
lessons.intro: Joseph was given a hard question by a king. His first words were that he could not answer it by himself. That is what depending on God's wisdom looks like.
lessons.notes:
Wisdom is knowing the right meaning and the right thing to do. Joseph did not pretend. Genesis 41:16 says, "I cannot do it." Then he pointed Pharaoh to God. The answer about plenty and famine was God's answer, given through Joseph.

### Lessons from the story
- Do not boast. Joseph refused to claim a power he did not have.
- Ask God for wisdom before you speak about things too big for you.
- God knows the future. The seven years were His plan made known to Pharaoh.
- Use God's gift to help people. The meaning of the dream warned Egypt about famine so the country could face it. Joseph loved God, and the warning was for the good of the land where he lived.
- A leader tells the truth even to a powerful person. Joseph told the king both the good years and the hard years.

### Depending on God in Grade 4
You are not asked to interpret a king's dream. You are asked to depend on God in smaller ways:

- Pray before a test, then study. Do not cheat.
- When friends ask you to decide something confusing, pray and ask a parent or teacher.
- If you do not know, say "I do not know" instead of inventing an answer. Joseph said he could not do it.
- Thank God when you understand a lesson.
- Use what you know to help the class, not to show off.

Share a dream you have had only as a personal story. Do not claim you know its secret meaning. The Bible's point is that God gave Pharaoh the meaning, not that every dream we have must be explained by us. Mention three lessons from Joseph and choose one to practise this week.

keyWords.meaning: knowing what is true and what is right to do
to rely on someone instead of trusting only yourself

activity.title: Three lessons from Joseph
steps: Mention three lessons learnt from Genesis 41:14-24 and 28-30.
In pairs, share a dream you have dreamt, without claiming a hidden meaning.
Say one way you will depend on God's wisdom this week.
Sing a song related to the story.

practice.question: How was Joseph able to interpret Pharaoh's dream?
practice.answer: He could not do it by himself. God gave Pharaoh the answer.

practice.question: State two lessons from the story.
practice.answer: Any two: do not boast; ask God for wisdom; God knows what is coming; use God's gift to help people; tell the truth to those in authority.

practice.question: What should you do when you do not know an answer?
practice.answer: Say that you do not know, pray, and ask God for wisdom instead of inventing an answer.

summary: Joseph depended on God and refused to take the credit.
God showed that seven plentiful years would be followed by famine.
We depend on God's wisdom by praying, telling the truth, and not pretending.

lessons.title: The fear of the LORD
objectives: Explain that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge and wisdom.
lessons.intro: Joseph feared God more than he feared looking weak before Pharaoh. Proverbs 1:7 says that this kind of fear is where knowledge begins.
lessons.notes:
Proverbs 1:7 says, "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction."

### What the fear of the LORD means
This fear is not the terror that makes you run from a cruel person. It is deep respect for God. You take Him seriously. You hate what He hates. You listen when He speaks. The learning outcome calls this the beginning of wisdom. The verse itself says the beginning of knowledge. Knowledge and wisdom belong together here: you start to know what is true, and you start to live wisely, when you reverence God.

A fool, in this verse, is not a person who cannot do sums. A fool is a person who looks down on wisdom and will not be taught. Joseph did the opposite. He let God teach him the meaning of the dream.

### How this fits Joseph
Joseph said, "I cannot do it," because he knew the interpretation belonged to God. That is the fear of the LORD. He did not despise God's instruction. He passed it on to Pharaoh, including the hard news about famine.

### Living it
- Recite Proverbs 1:7 every morning this week.
- Obey a correction from a parent or teacher. That is refusing to despise instruction.
- Pray before you make a choice.
- Do not laugh at someone who is trying to learn.
- Remember that wisdom starts with God, not with showing off.

When you fear the LORD, you can stand before a hard question the way Joseph stood before Pharaoh: humble, truthful, and sure that God gives wisdom.

keyWords.meaning: deep respect for God that takes Him seriously
teaching that shows you what to do

activity.title: Recite Proverbs 1:7
steps: Read Proverbs 1:7 and write it on a flash card.
Recite it until you can say it without looking.
Explain in your own words what the fear of the LORD means.
Say how Joseph showed this fear before Pharaoh.
Sing a song thanking God for wisdom.

practice.question: Recite Proverbs 1:7.
practice.answer: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

practice.question: What does the fear of the LORD mean in this verse?
practice.answer: Deep respect for God, taking Him seriously and listening to His instruction.

practice.question: How did Joseph show that he feared God?
practice.answer: He refused to claim the interpretation for himself and said God would give the answer.

summary: Proverbs 1:7: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.
This fear is deep respect, not panic.
Joseph showed it by giving God the credit for the interpretation.

quiz.question: Which passage tells of Joseph before Pharaoh in this sub-strand?
quiz.explanation: Those are the verses the class reads.

quiz.question: Joseph was brought from...
quiz.explanation: Genesis 41:14 says he was brought from the dungeon.

quiz.question: In the first dream, the thin cows...
quiz.explanation: Pharaoh said the thin, ugly cows ate the fat cows.

quiz.question: What did Joseph say he could not do?
quiz.answer: He could not interpret the dream by himself.
quiz.explanation: Genesis 41:16 says, "I cannot do it," and points Pharaoh to God.

quiz.question: The dreams meant...
options: seven years of plenty and then seven years of famine
quiz.explanation: Genesis 41:29-30 states the seven years of abundance and the seven years of famine.

quiz.question: Joseph was able to give the meaning because:
quiz.explanation: Joseph said God would give Pharaoh the answer he desired.

quiz.question: A learner who depends on God's wisdom will:
options: pray, tell the truth, and refuse to cheat
quiz.explanation: Depending on God includes honesty and prayer, as Joseph refused to take the credit.

quiz.question: Proverbs 1:7 says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of:
quiz.explanation: The verse says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.

quiz.question: The fear of the LORD in Proverbs 1:7 means:
quiz.answer: Deep respect for God that listens to wisdom and instruction.
quiz.explanation: It is not hatred of God, and it is not the same as panicking.

quiz.question: Fools, in Proverbs 1:7, are people who:
options: tell the truth to a king
quiz.explanation: The verse says fools despise wisdom and instruction.
